question: My home internet contract has an early cancellation fee. What minimum trial period does the CRTC Internet Code give me if my provider is covered?
generated_answer:
The CRTC Internet Code requires that providers give a minimum 30-day trial period for new customers. However, if your contract has an early cancellation fee, the provider can still charge this fee if you cancel during the trial period. The trial period is designed to give you time to test the service and decide if it meets your needs. If you cancel within the trial period, you may still be responsible for paying the early cancellation fee, even if you're within the 30-day window. It's important to review your contract carefully and understand the terms before signing up for a service.

If you're unsure about your specific situation or the terms of your contract, you may want to contact your provider directly to ask about their trial period and any associated fees. You can also reach out to the CRTC for guidance or to file a complaint if you believe your provider is not following the Internet Code.

Remember, the 30-day trial period is a minimum requirement, and some providers may offer longer trial periods or different terms. Always read and understand the terms of your contract before signing up for a service.
